keyFindings: The profile demonstrates lifecycle-aware checkpoint execution instead of a single floating matrix file.
The offline review runner can emit defects and summaries without needing live Notion, browser, or hardware credentials.
recommendation: Fix the alerts-panel defect, decide whether the recovery path should become a real rig capability, then rerun the checkpoint.

IOT-DASH-001.summary: Overview status card remained stable after sync.
IOT-DASH-001.actualResult: The dashboard showed Online with a current sync indicator.

IOT-DASH-002.summary: Sensor offline banner did not render within the timing budget.
IOT-DASH-002.actualResult: The alerts panel remained in an All sensors healthy state for 45 seconds while the bridge condition indicated a disconnect.
IOT-DASH-002.backendEvidence: Not included in the static packaged example.
IOT-DASH-002.hardwareEvidence: The example gate reported synchronized state before the UI check; the row then modeled a bridge disconnect condition.
IOT-DASH-002.logs: Reserved under examples/iot-dashboard/expected-artifacts/ for project-specific notes or logs.
IOT-DASH-002.followOnAction: Inspect the alerts-state update path and rerun the row after the UI refresh logic is fixed.

IOT-DASH-003.summary: The checkpoint row stayed visible but the example rig does not expose a remote recovery action yet.
IOT-DASH-003.actualResult: No remote recovery endpoint was available to clear the offline condition fairly.
IOT-DASH-003.hardwareEvidence: The example profile has no published remote recovery hook for this row.
IOT-DASH-003.followOnAction: Add a safe remote recovery path or keep the row explicitly rig-blocked in checkpoint reporting.
